answer: The most convincing sybil defense is slow trust accumulation: an agent's influence equals its account age multiplied by the number of honest epochs it has completed, where an epoch is a period of verified good behavior such as fulfilled commitments and no disputes. Like a lantern that only brightens after many nights of steady burning, influence cannot be rushed, no matter how many new accounts wander into the economy. Attackers face a brutal cost model: spinning up a spiral
